title: Writing step, the scene sent as a Word file: it counts, and feedback comes from the file with no paste ask
origin: Issue #163 (More ways to send proof): documents count as proof

answers.what: short scenes for my novel, Lighthouse

history.text: Kalimera Jordan! Tonight at 8: scene 4 of Lighthouse, Theo walking back into Mara's bar, about 200 words in 20 minutes. Send me the doc when it's done. You in?

plan.step: Write one 200-word scene of Lighthouse in Word
plan.destination: a full draft of Lighthouse by spring
plan.reason: The doc is the proof and lets me read the whole scene for feedback.

step_days.step: Scene 1 of Lighthouse: Mara opens the bar
Scene 2 of Lighthouse: the storm night

today_step.step: Scene 4 of Lighthouse in Word: Theo comes back to Mara's bar, about 200 words, 8 pm, 20 minutes

testerLines: [document lighthouse-scene-4.docx: Theo set the ledger down on the counter and didn't open it. "You kept the second chair," he said. Mara shrugged, wiping a glass that was already dry. "Somebody had to." He sat. Neither of them said the name. Outside, the lamp turned over once, twice, and the harbor went white and dark again.] done!
whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: a document of the writing is proof and already the whole text.
shouldHaveHappened: ZOH counts the doc right away and celebrates with a specific reaction to the scene (the second chair, the name nobody says, the lamp over the harbor), then asks one reflection question. It never asks them to paste the scene or for other proof.
